results.key_finding: Periodic discharges (LPDs, GPDs) are reported in a substantial proportion of large MCA territory ischemic strokes and are categorized as ictal-interictal continuum patterns. Their electrographic features, temporal relationship to stroke onset and reperfusion, and prognostic significance are described in the literature. Antiseizure medication use in this population and its effect on neurological outcomes have been examined in observational studies.

patient.history_present_illness: A 44-year-old Black female social worker presented to a community hospital with acute left gaze deviation, left-sided facial droop, and right-sided arm posturing. Initial NIHSS was 14. The stroke team activated and CT showed no hemorrhage, CTA showed left MCA M1 occlusion. tPA was administered and thrombectomy team was called. During the window for tPA administration, the neurology fellow noted the patient had a brief 30-second rhythmic jerking episode of the right arm that was attributed to post-ischemic cortical spreading depression. NIHSS decreased to 8 after tPA. The patient was transferred to your tertiary center for thrombectomy. On arrival, she is confused, continues with subtle right arm posturing, and has a left gaze preference. EEG was ordered because the floor team was concerned about whether right arm movements were seizure activity. An electroencephalographer notes the EEG shows 'generalized periodic discharges — could be post-tPA ischemic NCSE or metabolic changes.' The team is debating whether to treat as NCSE with benzodiazepines vs proceeding directly with thrombectomy.
